beliefs.practice: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment at runtime, never write it to logs, files, or checked-in config; provide only a .env.example placeholder.
Use a single shared Mongoose connection (initialized once at app start) with connection pooling (set maxPoolSize) and reuse that connection across modules instead of creating per-request connections.

Provide explicit Mongoose/MongoClient connection options to avoid long waits: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g. 10_000), socketTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize (e.g. 50), and useUnifiedTopology/autoEncryption options appropriate for the driver version.
Force TLS and verify certificates in the connection string/options (tls=true / ssl=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so traffic to DocumentDB is encrypted and verified.
Don't commit LLM API keys: default the sample to mock-LLM mode unless OPENAI_API_KEY (or equivalent) is present in env, and read keys only from environment or a secure secrets store.

Model the return document and order using explicit Mongoose schemas with validation and typed fields (required, enums, max length) and use lean() for read-only queries to avoid Mongoose document overhead.

Create concrete indexes for the query patterns used by the orchestration: an index on { orderId: 1 } or { customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 } and any compound indexes used by the policy/refund queries to avoid COLLSCANs.

If storing embeddings for vector search, create a vector index with explicit method/params (e.g. HNSW with m and efConstruction tuned) and store embedding dimension in index metadata; restrict vector search with metadata filters to reduce candidate set.
When doing vector similarity queries, set an appropriate ef (efSearch/ef) and topK parameters on the search call to trade recall vs latency; tune these based on measured latency and RU consumption.
Use projections to fetch only the fields each agent needs (e.g., policy agent only needs order items, dates, return policy fields) rather than fetching whole documents.

Make writes idempotent or include an idempotency key for return creation so retry logic (backoff/retry) cannot create duplicate returns; enforce a unique index on returnId or (orderId, returnAttemptId).
Implement exponential backoff + jitter for transient Mongo/DocumentDB errors (network/server selection, 50x, 429) and fail fast on unrecoverable errors; record retry attempts in logs/metrics.
When calling external LLM services, wrap calls with timeouts and circuit-breaker logic and fall back to a safe deterministic mode (mock responses) in the sample to avoid blocking the orchestration.

Provision and monitor throughput (RU/s) or use autoscale for the sample_retail_18 database/collections and monitor RU consumption during seeding and demo scripts to avoid 429s; scale up for load-sensitive operations like vector search.

Verify indexes and query plans against the live cluster (use listIndexes and explain()) during development and include a script (scripts/list-indexes.js) that runs these checks against sample_retail_18.

Avoid multi-document transactions across many partitions; prefer single-document updates or application-level reconciliation; if using transactions, keep them short and targeted and test their support on the target wire protocol.
Use collection-level JSON Schema validation where available to enforce basic invariants (required fields, types) so malformed returns/orders are rejected by the DB.
Tune index cardinality and consider partial/sparse indexes for fields that are present only on some documents (e.g., 'refund.calculatedAt') to reduce index size and RU cost.
Keep large LLM-generated content out of hot documents: store long notifications or transcripts in a separate blob storage or a separate collection/document with its own lifecycle/indexing policy.
Use audit fields (createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy, changeReason) on return documents and index createdAt for retention/cleanup jobs; consider TTL indexes for ephemeral data.
Instrument and emit metrics for latency, RU consumption, index hit/miss, and error rates for the orchestration flow so you can tune indexes, pool sizes and vector search params in production.
Sanitize and validate any user-provided query parameters to avoid NoSQL injection (do not interpolate user input into query operators like $expr, $where, or pipeline stages without validation).

When running seed/demo scripts against sample_retail_18, ensure they only operate on that database and include an explicit confirmation or environment check to avoid accidental destructive ops on other DBs.

If the MongoDB wire protocol version/feature set is uncertain, set retryWrites=false and explicitly test features used (transactions, change streams, collations, vector functions) against the live cluster to detect incompatibilities.

Keep Mongoose and MongoDB driver versions aligned with the cluster wire protocol (e.g., MongoDB 7.0 compatibility declared by the cluster) and test driver-level features (schema validation, index creation syntax, vector index commands) on the target environment.
